description: PR #9 (the verifier and thread lifecycle) at its first pushed commit, as replayed in the buggrit#8 model trial: the 7 defects reviewers raised on e619281 and fixed later in #9, plus the 3 real extra findings from that trial, filed as #13-#15.
head: e61928194c1995a6743b2eedde530c0480206313
title: Verify earlier findings and drive each thread through its lifecycle
body:
## Summary

Build step 4, first of two PRs: the **verifier and the thread lifecycle** (design §6, §7 rules 4 and 6). buggrit now checks its earlier findings on every run, judges replies, and moves each thread through `open → fixed / dismissed / needs_human`. It resolves, unresolves and repairs threads behind the head fence.

- **`internal/state`**
  - Transition markers gain `kind`, `seen` (the newest human comment handled) and `left_resolved`.
  - `Replay` reads a finding's state, rebuttal count and unhandled replies from its thread. Only buggrit's own markers count; every other comment is a human's.
  - `Next` is the §6 state machine. It's a pure function, table-tested.
- **`internal/review`**
  - The tool loop (nudge, wrap-up, transcript repair) moves to `stage.go`, shared by the finder and the new **verifier** stage. The verifier has `get_thread` and the `submit_verdicts` terminal tool.
  - `selectChecks` implements §6's selection rules. Fixed findings are re-verified when an evidence file changed, or when the fix commit left the branch history.
  - In a full pass, verify and find **run at once and share the pass deadline**. The limiter decides how many calls actually overlap.
- **`internal/publish`**
  - Each transition is posted as a reply with its marker, followed by resolve or unresolve, with the fence checked before each mutation.
  - A refused resolution is listed in the review body for a human to do by hand.
  - The finding footer is now the §8 target text, with an advisory variant that offers dismissal.
- **`cmd/buggrit`**: wires up both stage clients, prints transitions in `--dry-run`, adds a verify row to the job summary, and exits 1 when earlier findings were left unverified.

## Design references

- [§6 Finding state machine](docs/design.md#finding-state-machine): "every `open` and `needs_human` finding, including resolved threads, because resolving isn't proof." Every run, reconcile-only included, verifies all of them.
- §6: "The one thing that never settles a finding is **a bare resolution with no reply while the issue is still present**." That case gets a `reopened` transition. buggrit never repeats a transition when no human has commented since; it only repairs.
- §6, new: "**A needs_human thread is unresolved before its marker lands.**" Replay reads a resolution under that marker as a human settling the finding, so the unresolve is always sent first.
- [§6 Review baseline](docs/design.md#review-baseline): the pass marker's status "follows the finder". Re-running the finder over a scope it already searched is the drip-feed that incremental scope exists to stop. Unverified findings make the run `incomplete` (exit 1), and the next run picks them up.
- §7 rule 4: "For **advisory** findings (P2/P3), any reasoned reply … is accepted as a dismissal without a rebuttal."
- §9: "Running them together is an optimization, not a requirement."

## What this PR does NOT do

- **Reply-triggered runs.** The `pull_request_review_comment` and `pull_request_review` triggers, and the bot-event concurrency group (§3), arrive in the next PR. The dogfood workflow builds from `main`, so they only become useful once this PR has merged.
- **Reopening a fixed finding when the finder re-raises its fingerprint** (§7 rule 3) waits for step 5's dedupe. For now that finding is dropped as already raised. The verifier still reopens a regression when its evidence files change.
- **Summary comment, JSON ledger, non-convergence warning and gate check:** step 5.
- **Skipping untouched findings on a reconcile-only rerun.** Every run re-verifies every open finding. A correct skip needs a per-finding record of the last head each was verified at, which goes in step 5's ledger (§2).

## Test plan

- `make check` passes: golangci-lint, govulncheck, build, and `go test -cover -race ./...`. Coverage: review 93%, state 95%, publish 91%.
- Multi-pass scenarios from §11 run against `githubtest`, in `internal/publish/lifecycle_test.go`:
  - fix, then regression through a changed evidence file;
  - false resolve, then a repeat resolve that unresolves without a new reply;
  - an invalid rebuttal, then `needs_human`, then settling by a reply or by a resolution;
  - a valid rebuttal; an advisory reply;
  - a publish killed between the reply and the resolve, repaired on the next run;
  - the head moving mid-publish;
  - resolve refused by GitHub;
  - verification cut short, then checked on the next run;
  - a force-push back to a reviewed head;
  - a killed or refused `needs_human` unresolve; the thread resolved while the verifier runs.
- Mutation checks by hand: reverting each `needs_human` fix makes its test fail.
- Codex reviewed three rounds through Counterpoint and approved `e619281`.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

defects.description: Pending means newer than Seen, not newer than the needs_human marker: a reply that arrives during verification can precede the marker yet stay pending, so NeedsSettling settles the finding on a reply the verifier already handled.
An advisory finding is dismissed on any new reply, even when the verifier returns open after disproving the reply (for example a false "fixed in abc123").
With leftResolved set, NeedsSettling ignores resolutions and requires a reply, but the needs_human footer still promises that a resolution settles the finding.
If GitHub refuses the initial needs_human unresolve, the marker records LeftResolved=true, so NeedsSettling stays false without a new reply and the unresolve is never retried.
CLAUDE.md's directory layout and the dogfood workflow's comment still describe the pre-verifier build (internal/state as markers only, the verifier as future work).
A resolve or unresolve GitHub refuses in a reconcile-only run is never reported on the PR: Publish returns before posting the review body, the only place the manual list appears.
--dry-run prints a needs_human transition's reply and unresolve in the opposite order to publishing, and always says left_resolved.
earlier() counts a repair-only transition as both "repaired" and "unchanged": changed[id] is set only for a transition with a Kind.
Design §6's state machine diagram has no needs_human → fixed edge, though state.Next emits KindFixed for a needs_human finding verified fixed.

The verifier's opening message isn't held strictly to the 300 KiB budget: the findings section is capped from its own start, pending replies per finding are uncapped, and get_thread checks its limit only after appending a comment.
